sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Central Sector Schemes (CSS)**: 100% funded by the Union Government and implemented through Central Government machinery or agencies.
• **Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSSS)**: Implemented by State Governments with funding shared between the Centre and States (typically 60:40 for general states, 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan states).
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**: Mechanism introduced to transfer subsidies and welfare benefits directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries, minimizing leakages.
• **Output vs. Outcome Monitoring**: Shift from tracking physical and financial inputs/outputs to measuring real socio-economic impact and behavioral shifts.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP)**: Targets 112 underdeveloped districts across backward states (Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha, Chhattisgarh) using convergence and competition.
• **Vibrant Villages Programme**: Focuses on comprehensive development of select border villages in northern border regions to stem outmigration.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Delayed fund transfers by states, exclusion errors, ghost beneficiaries, and administrative capacity gaps.
• **Policy Interventions**: Rationalization of schemes into umbrella programs, Aadhaar-biometric authentication, and outcome-linked budget allocations.

items.title: Mnemonic for CSS Funding Ratio (General vs NE/Himalayan)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: '60-40 General Election, 90-10 Nine-Ten School'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: General states share is 60:40 (Centre:State); North-Eastern and Himalayan states share is 90:10.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly catches examiner traps where funding patterns are deliberately inverted.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: If a scheme is implemented by Central Ministries directly without State machinery, it is 100% Central Sector, never Centrally Sponsored.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that all welfare schemes are 100% funded by the Central Government. Always check whether a scheme is Centrally Sponsored (requires State matching share) or Central Sector.
Mains Value Addition: Emphasize the trinity of JAM (Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile) as the technological bedrock that transformed scheme delivery efficiency and plugged fiscal leakages.

keyTakeaways: Government schemes are broadly classified into Central Sector (100% Centre) and Centrally Sponsored Schemes (shared funding).
Digital public infrastructure like PFMS and DBT have revolutionized fund tracking and eliminated intermediaries.
UPSC Prelims heavily tests funding ratios, implementing ministries, and statutory backing, while Mains evaluates socio-economic outcomes.
